messages.author: cd0529e92db343cb
messages.subject: CSV Import format?
parts:
I am new to R and to unmarked, so it's possible that I am asking this incorrectly.

I have a collection of camera trap data in csv format. I want to then analyse it in R with unmarked.
I reviewed the help files, and everything else that I could find, I could not determine how to import my data and in what format it should be.
I'm using different software to collect my information in CSV, eg:
headers: filename, species, species#, latitude, longitude, timestamp, etc

Is there a specific format CSV that I should/could be using in order to quickly import it into R for unmarked?
If so, what would it be?

Thanks

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] CSV Import format?
parts:
Dear Heidi,
 You should be able to read your data into R using read.csv or other standard R input functions (this is not specific to unmarked).

 Each class of models in unmarked has a data packaging function to package the data into an unmarkedFrame data structure.  For example if you wish to fit occupancy models you can look at the help file ?occu for an example involving the frog survey data.  You can understand the data structure by going through line-by-line and checking each result out. 
 The Applied Hierarchical Modeling book that was just published has detailed worked examples of many classes of models from unmarked.

regards,
andy

messages.author: 39971e2c19b8ec70
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] CSV Import format?
parts:
Dear Heidi,

I am using read.csv2() fujction to load data into R. You usually need some more data transforming magic to be able to transform the data into the shape needed by unmarked. This is often not trivial and needs some deeper experience with R. If you post an R question on stackoverflow.com though, you get very good answers on R within minutes. I use this all the time.
Also, if you by chance know SQL, you can do almost any data transformation with sqldf() function.

Tomas

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: CSV Import format?
parts:
hi Heidi,
 I would recommend that you look at the examples in many of the help files for the various functions (?occu ?pcount) and study the data structures used in those examples. In short: you can make progress by mimicking exactly how those data files look.  I don't know how to better answer the question because there is not a single unique answer (depends on the model you're interested in, the objectives, the specific questions you have, etc..).
 I would also recommend watching this webinar which has some examples:
 A 5 hour "introduction to unmarked" Webinar can be found here: http://www.pwrc.usgs.gov/Roylevideo.cfm
regards
andy
